'''Tonty Enmanuel''' "'''Manny'''" '''Rutinel''' (born December 20, 1994)<ref>{{Cite tweet |last=Rutinel |first=Manny |user=MannyRutinel |number=1737534902097043783 |date=December 20, 2023 |title=It's my birthday! I've spent it the best way I know how: Chatting with @jaredpolis about how we can fight for our environment, public health, and working families. Excited about the policies we'll be passing for Coloradans next session! ⛰️ |language=en |access-date=January 28, 2025}}</ref><ref name="copol co08">{{cite news |last1=Luning |first1=Ernest |title=Democratic state lawmaker Manny Rutinel launches bid to challenge Gabe Evans in Colorado's 8th CD |url=https://www.coloradopolitics.com/elections/democratic-state-lawmaker-manny-rutinel-launches-bid-to-challenge-gabe-evans-in-colorados-8th-cd/article_585bfab4-dcf1-11ef-bb61-7bedbcbcb97a.html |access-date=January 28, 2025 |work=Colorado Politics |date=January 27, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> is an American attorney and politician who served as a member of the [[Colorado House of Representatives]] for the [[Colorado's 32nd House of Representatives district|32nd district]] from 2023 to 2026.

Rutinel was the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee for {{ushr|CO|8}} in [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Colorado#District_8|the 2026 election]], defeating incumbent [[Gabe Evans]] in the general.

== Early life and education ==
Rutinel was born in Los Angeles, California, in 1994 and raised by a single mother in the [[Dominican Republic]] until he was six years old.<ref>{{cite news |title=Law students to law firms: kick Exxon to the curb or sashay away|url=https://www.exxonknews.org/p/law-students-to-law-firms-kick-exxon |access-date=June 4, 2026 |work=ExxonKnews |date=March 6, 2020}}</ref>{{#tag:ref|His paternal family is an influential political dynasty in the Dominican Republic. His estranged father, Tonty Rutinel, is a politician and diplomat from the Dominican Republic who was Senator (2002–2006) and Representative (1990–2002 and 2020–2024), and currently serves as Consul-General to Bogotá, Colombia since 2024; he unsuccessfully ran for mayor of [[Santo Domingo Este]] in the 2010 and 2016 elections. His paternal grandmother, Francisca Otilia Domínguez (1923–2010), was a leader in the failed [[Dominican Civil War|April Revolution of 1965]] and later became Consul-General of the D.R. in Haiti and Panama; she was a cousin of President [[Hipólito Mejía]]. Abelardo Rutinel, a cousin of Manny, is a congressman of the D.R. since 2024. His uncle José Ulises Rutinel was a professor and Dean of the Faculty of Philosophy of the [[Autonomous University of Santo Domingo]].<ref>{{cite news |title= Manny Rutinel, hijo de «Tonty» aventaja por 15.7 puntos a republicano en Colorado |newspaper= El Nuevo Diario |date= November 3, 2026 |page= |edition= |url= https://elnuevodiario.com.do/manny-rutinel-hijo-de-tonty-aventaja-por-15-7-puntos-a-republicano-en-colorado/ |via= |access-date= |language=es }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title= Tonty Rutinel elegido por 5ta vez legislador, tras 14 años alejado del Congreso |newspaper= El Nuevo Diario |date= July 9, 2020 |page= |edition= |url= https://elnuevodiario.com.do/tonty-rutinel-elegido-por-5ta-vez-legislador-tras-14-anos-alejado-del-congreso/ |via= |access-date= |language=es }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Doña Francisca Otilia Domínguez fue sepultada |newspaper= Hoy |date= August 12, 2013 |page= |edition= |url= https://hoy.com.do/el-pais/dona-francisca-otilia-dominguez-fue-sepultada_344637.html |via= |access-date= |language=es }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title= La "modernización" de Juancito contra la "descentralización" de Tonty en SDE  |newspaper= Diario Libre |date= May 13, 2010 |page= |edition= |url=https://www.diariolibre.com/actualidad/la-modernizacin-de-juancito-contra-la-descentralizacin-de-tonty-en-sde-NODL245181 |via= |access-date= |language=es }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title= Tonty Rutinel: De ser el legislador que divide el territorio, a cónsul en Colombia |newspaper=[[Listín Diario]] |date= August 24, 2024 |page= |edition= |url= https://web.archive.org/web/20240828071816/https://listindiario.com/la-republica/congreso/20240824/tonty-rutinel-legislador-divide-territorio-consul-colombia_822789.html |via= |access-date= |language=es }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title= De Santo Domingo a Washington: el legado de una familia al servicio de dos naciones |newspaper= Diario La Verdad |date= July 1, 2026 |page= |edition= |url=https://www.rdlaverdad.com/2026/07/de-santo-domingo-a-washington-el-legado-de-una-familia-al-servicio-de-dos-naciones/ |via= |access-date= |language=es }}</ref> |group=nb}} They returned to the United States and lived in [[California]] and [[Florida]]. He attended schools in Florida.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Better |first1=Rossana Longo |title=Rep. Manny Rutinel looks to represent Commerce City's drive for economic, environmental justice |url=https://coloradocommunitymedia.com/2024/02/14/rep-manny-rutinel-looks-to-represent-commerce-citys-drive-for-economic-environmental-justice/ |access-date=January 27, 2025 |work=Commerce City Sentinel Express |date=February 14, 2024}}</ref> He stated that he worked at [[McDonald's]] while attending high school and regularly gave blood at a plasma center to help support his family.<ref name="copol co08" />

Rutinel earned an associate degree from [[Pasco–Hernando State College]], a Bachelor of Arts in economics and Bachelor of Science in microbiology from the [[University of Florida]], a Master of Science in applied economics from [[Johns Hopkins University]], and a Juris Doctor from [[Yale Law School]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilson |first=Sara |date=October 2, 2023 |title=Colorado Democrats pick Manny Rutinel to take vacant seat in Legislature |url=https://coloradonewsline.com/briefs/colorado-democrats-manny-rutinel-vacancy-legislature/ |access-date=2023-10-06 |website=Colorado Newsline |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Career ==
[[File:Manny rutinel.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Rutinel in 2025]]
From 2016 to 2018, Rutinel served as an economist for the [[United States Army Corps of Engineers]] in [[Upstate New York]].<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |title=Army engineers provide power for critical public facilities in Puerto Rico after hurricanes |url=https://www.army.mil/article/199124/army_engineers_provide_power_for_critical_public_facilities_in_puerto_rico_after_hurricanes |access-date=2023-10-06 |website=army.mil |language=en}}</ref> Rutinel served as a first responder in [[Puerto Rico]] after [[Hurricane Maria]].<ref name="Website-1" /> After graduating from law school, he worked as an associate attorney at [[Earthjustice]]. Since 2021, Rutinel has worked as the CEO of Climate Refarm, a non-profit organization. Rutinel was introduced to Colorado politics working for Senator John Hickenlooper's campaign in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-10-22 |title=Manny Rutinel leans hard into anti-Trumpism in 8th District race — while pivoting away from his activist past |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2026/10/22/manny-rutinel-8th-congressional-district-race/ |access-date=2026-10-23 |website=The Denver Post |language=en-US}}</ref> 

In October 2023, he was selected to fill the former seat of [[Dafna Michaelson Jenet]] in the Colorado House of Representatives. She had been selected for a vacant state senate seat.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodland |first=Marianne |date=2023-10-02 |title=Adams County Democrats pick Manny Rutinel for House vacancy |url=https://www.coloradopolitics.com/news/tonty-manny-rutinel-democrats-house-district-32-election/article_4b497566-6152-11ee-b8ab-7730088790ec.html |access-date=2023-10-06 |website=Colorado Politics |language=en}}</ref> In 2024, [[2024 Colorado House of Representatives election#District 32|Rutinel won reelection]] to the seat.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Manny Rutinel |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Manny_Rutinel |access-date=2026-10-24 |website=Ballotpedia |language=en}}</ref> Rutinel has led legislative efforts to conduct oversight of [[ICE]] detention centers in Colorado.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salzman |first=Jason |date=2026-03-06 |title=After CO Times Recorder Revealed Secret Detention Centers in CO, 31 Lawmakers Call on ICE for ‘Immediate Transparency’ |url=https://coloradotimesrecorder.com/2026/03/after-co-times-recorder-revealed-secret-detention-centers-in-co-27-lawmakers-call-on-ice-for-immediate-transparency/77113/ |access-date=2026-04-11 |website=Colorado Times Recorder |language=en}}</ref> 

On January 27, 2025, Rutinel announced that he would run for the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Colorado#District 8|2026 U.S. House of Representatives election]] in [[Colorado's 8th congressional district]], seeking to unseat Republican incumbent [[Gabe Evans]].<ref name="co082026">{{cite news |last1=Woodruff |first1=Chase |title=State Rep. Manny Rutinel running for Congress in Colorado's battleground 8th District |url=https://coloradonewsline.com/briefs/manny-rutinel-congress-8th-district/ |access-date=January 27, 2025 |work=Colorado Newsline |date=January 27, 2025}}</ref> On September 4, 2026, Rutinel resigned from his seat in order to focus on his campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.coloradopolitics.com/2026/09/04/manny-rutinel-resigns-from-colorado-legislature-to-focus-on-congressional-race/|title=Manny Rutinel resigns from Colorado legislature to focus on congressional race|last=Ventrelli|first=Marissa|date=September 4, 2026|access-date=September 4, 2026|website=[[The Colorado Statesman|Colorado Politics]]}}</ref> The race for Colorado's 8th Congressional District between Rutinel and Evans is the highest spending campaign in Colorado (as of October 2026) for the 2026 elections with about $11 million spent by outside organizations between the June 30 primary and October 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kim |first=Caitlyn |date=2026-10-07 |title=Candidates, outside groups spending big on Colorado’s congressional races |url=https://www.cpr.org/2026/10/07/colorado-congressional-race-spending/ |access-date=2026-10-15 |website=Colorado Public Radio |language=en}}</ref>

== Political positions ==

=== Social issues ===
Rutinel supports tax credits for working parents and higher taxes on billionaires.<ref name="Paul2">{{Cite web |last=Paul|first=Jesse|last2=Eason|first2=Brian|date=2026-10-21|title=Where Gabe Evans, Manny Rutinel stand on the key issues in the 8th Congressional District|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/21/manny-rutinel-gabe-evans-voter-guide-colorado-district-8/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Kim1">{{Cite web |last=Kim |first=Caitlyn |date=2026-09-25 |title=8th Congressional District: Democrat Manny Rutinel |url=https://www.cpr.org/2026/09/25/vg-2026-manny-rutinel-voter-guide/ |access-date=2026-10-23 |website=Colorado Public Radio |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Dolven1">{{Cite web |last=Dolven |first=Taylor |date=2026-05-28 |title=Where Shannon Bird and Manny Rutinel stand on the issues in Colorado’s 8th Congressional District primary |url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/05/28/manny-rutinel-shannon-bird-colorado-primary-issue-guide/ |access-date=2026-10-23 |website=The Colorado Sun |language=en-US}}</ref> Rutinel supports protecting [[Social Security (United States)|Social Security]] and [[Medicare (United States)|Medicare]].<ref name="Paul2" /><ref name="Kim1" /><ref name="Website-12">{{Cite web |date=2026-10-22 |title=Manny Rutinel leans hard into anti-Trumpism in 8th District race — while pivoting away from his activist past |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2026/10/22/manny-rutinel-8th-congressional-district-race/ |access-date=2026-10-23 |website=The Denver Post |language=en-US}}</ref> Rutinel supports removing the taxable income cap for contributions to social security to continue to fund the program.<ref name="Paul2" />

=== Technology and AI ===
Rutinel supports the regulation of [[Artificial intelligence|AI]], whistleblower protections, and transparency rules for AI models.<ref name="Paul22">{{Cite web |last=Paul|first=Jesse|last2=Eason|first2=Brian|date=2026-10-21|title=Where Gabe Evans, Manny Rutinel stand on the key issues in the 8th Congressional District|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/21/manny-rutinel-gabe-evans-voter-guide-colorado-district-8/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Dolven12">{{Cite web |last=Dolven|first=Taylor|date=2026-05-28|title=Where Shannon Bird and Manny Rutinel stand on the issues in Colorado’s 8th Congressional District primary|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/05/28/manny-rutinel-shannon-bird-colorado-primary-issue-guide/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Lerer1">{{Cite news |last=Lerer |first=Lisa |date=2026-10-20 |title=A High-Tech Debate in Cattle Country |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/20/us/politics/colorado-elections-ai.html |access-date=2026-10-23 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Rutinel cosponsored a 2024 bill in the Colorado legislature that attempted to regulate use of AI for corporate discrimination.<ref name="Lerer1" />

=== Agriculture ===
Rutinel has publicly raised questions about the production and consumption of meat and dairy products since his time as a student in Florida.<ref name="Paul1">{{Cite web |last=Paul|first=Jesse|date=2025-10-22|title=Manny Rutinel has said a lot about the meat and dairy industries. Now he wants to represent Colorado’s ag capital in Congress.|url=https://coloradosun.com/2025/10/22/manny-rutinel-animal-activism-congressional-bid/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2016, he posed shirtless on draped in a banner for the [[People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals|People for Ethical Treatment of Animals]] while a student in Florida.<ref name="Paul1" /><ref name="Young1">{{Cite web |last=Young|first=Quentin|date=2026-08-13|title=Commentary: Colorado candidate says his positions have evolved. Voters might be skeptical.|url=https://coloradonewsline.com/2026/08/13/manny-rutinel-voters-might-be-skeptical/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=Colorado Newsline|language=en-US}}</ref> In a publication from Yale during his time as a law student, Rutinel is quoted as saying that "the globe must dramatically shift away from animal products and towards fruits, vegetables, legumes, whole grains, and nuts" while citing a study on climate change.<ref name="Paul1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-18|title=Rutinel & Animal Agriculture Legislation|url=https://www.agpros.com/articles-and-information/rutinel-testifies-for-legislation-calling-for-a-shift-away-from-animal-agriculture|access-date=2026-10-23|website=www.agpros.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-28|title=Q&A with Manny Rutinel ’22 on Carbon Offsets and Farming {{!}} Yale Law School|url=https://law.yale.edu/yls-today/news/qa-manny-rutinel-22-carbon-offsets-and-farming|access-date=2026-10-23|website=law.yale.edu|language=en}}</ref><ref name="Dolven2">{{Cite web |last=Dolven |first=Taylor |last2=Paul |first2=Jesse |date=2026-06-04 |title=Less than a year ago, Manny Rutinel staked out different positions on healthcare, student debt and fracking |url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/06/04/manny-rutinel-changed-positions-healthcare-student-debt-fracking/ |access-date=2026-10-23 |website=The Colorado Sun |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Young1" /> Rutinel has made comments that his views on agriculture are nuanced and he opposes bad actors but not the industry as a whole.<ref name="Paul1" /><ref name="Website-13">{{Cite web |date=2026-10-22|title=Manny Rutinel leans hard into anti-Trumpism in 8th District race — while pivoting away from his activist past|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2026/10/22/manny-rutinel-8th-congressional-district-race/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Denver Post|language=en-US}}</ref> Rutinel opposes tariffs put in place by President Donald Trump due to the financial impact on farmers and ranchers.<ref name="Paul1" />

=== Climate change ===
Rutinel was appointed to the Energy and Environment Committee in the Colorado House of Representatives for the 2024-2025 session.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Energy and Environment Committee, Colorado House of Representatives|url=https://ballotpedia.org/Energy_and_Environment_Committee,_Colorado_House_of_Representatives|access-date=2026-10-23|website=Ballotpedia|language=en}}</ref> Rutinel supports climate action and supports federal tax credits for renewable energy.<ref name="Paul23">{{Cite web |last=Paul|first=Jesse|last2=Eason|first2=Brian|date=2026-10-21|title=Where Gabe Evans, Manny Rutinel stand on the key issues in the 8th Congressional District|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/21/manny-rutinel-gabe-evans-voter-guide-colorado-district-8/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Kim12">{{Cite web |last=Kim|first=Caitlyn|date=2026-09-25|title=8th Congressional District: Democrat Manny Rutinel|url=https://www.cpr.org/2026/09/25/vg-2026-manny-rutinel-voter-guide/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=Colorado Public Radio|language=en}}</ref> Rutinel formerly supported a ban on fracking but no longer supports this position.<ref name="Dolven22">{{Cite web |last=Dolven|first=Taylor|last2=Paul|first2=Jesse|date=2026-06-04|title=Less than a year ago, Manny Rutinel staked out different positions on healthcare, student debt and fracking|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/06/04/manny-rutinel-changed-positions-healthcare-student-debt-fracking/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Healthcare ===
Rutinel opposes high health care costs and supports negotiations to lower pharmaceutical costs.<ref name="Paul24">{{Cite web |last=Paul|first=Jesse|last2=Eason|first2=Brian|date=2026-10-21|title=Where Gabe Evans, Manny Rutinel stand on the key issues in the 8th Congressional District|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/21/manny-rutinel-gabe-evans-voter-guide-colorado-district-8/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Dolven13">{{Cite web |last=Dolven|first=Taylor|date=2026-05-28|title=Where Shannon Bird and Manny Rutinel stand on the issues in Colorado’s 8th Congressional District primary|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/05/28/manny-rutinel-shannon-bird-colorado-primary-issue-guide/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref> He also is in favor of protecting [[Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program|SNAP]] access. Rutinel supports a public health insurance option.<ref name="Paul24" /><ref name="Kim13">{{Cite web |last=Kim|first=Caitlyn|date=2026-09-25|title=8th Congressional District: Democrat Manny Rutinel|url=https://www.cpr.org/2026/09/25/vg-2026-manny-rutinel-voter-guide/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=Colorado Public Radio|language=en}}</ref><ref name="Website-14">{{Cite web |date=2026-10-22|title=Manny Rutinel leans hard into anti-Trumpism in 8th District race — while pivoting away from his activist past|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2026/10/22/manny-rutinel-8th-congressional-district-race/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Denver Post|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Dolven23">{{Cite web |last=Dolven|first=Taylor|last2=Paul|first2=Jesse|date=2026-06-04|title=Less than a year ago, Manny Rutinel staked out different positions on healthcare, student debt and fracking|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/06/04/manny-rutinel-changed-positions-healthcare-student-debt-fracking/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Dolven13" />

=== Immigration ===
Rutinel supports pathways to citizenship for people formerly covered under [[Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals|DACA]].<ref name="Paul25">{{Cite web |last=Paul|first=Jesse|last2=Eason|first2=Brian|date=2026-10-21|title=Where Gabe Evans, Manny Rutinel stand on the key issues in the 8th Congressional District|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/21/manny-rutinel-gabe-evans-voter-guide-colorado-district-8/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Birkeland1">{{Cite web |last=Birkeland|first=Bente|date=2026-10-07|title=Gabe Evans and Manny Rutinel hold fiery debate in Colorado congressional swing seat race|url=https://www.cpr.org/2026/10/07/debate-8th-congressional-district-rutinel-evans/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=Colorado Public Radio|language=en}}</ref> He also supports citizenship options for immigrants who came to the United States illegally if they have been in the country for many years and been paying taxes.<ref name="Paul25" /><ref name="Kim14">{{Cite web Rutinel|url=https://www.cpr.org/2026/09/25/vg-2026-manny-rutinel-voter-guide/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=Colorado Public Radio|language=en}}</ref><ref name="Birkeland1" /><ref methods used by [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|immigration enforcement]] in the United States.<ref name="Kim14" /><ref name="Website-15">{{Cite web |date=2026-10-22|title=Manny Rutinel leans hard into anti-Trumpism in 8th District race — while pivoting away from his activist past|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2026/10/22/manny-rutinel-8th-congressional-district-race/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Denver Post|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Dolven14" />

=== Foreign policy ===
Rutinel supports U.S. financial support to [[Ukraine]].<ref name="Paul26">{{Cite web |last=Paul|first=Jesse|last2=Eason|first2=Brian|date=2026-10-21|title=Where Gabe Evans, Manny Rutinel stand on the key issues in the 8th Congressional District|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/21/manny-rutinel-gabe-evans-voter-guide-colorado-district-8/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref> He supports defending Israel as a US ally.<ref name="Paul26" /><ref name="Dolven15">{{Cite web |last=Dolven |first=Taylor |date=2026-05-28 |title=Where Shannon Bird and Manny Rutinel stand on the issues in Colorado’s 8th Congressional District primary |language=en-US |access-date=2026-10-23|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/05/28/manny-rutinel-shannon-bird-colorado-primary-issue-guide/|website=The Colorado Sun}}</ref><ref name="Website-16">{{Cite web |date=2026-10-22|title=Manny Rutinel leans hard into anti-Trumpism in 8th District race — while pivoting away from his activist past|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2026/10/22/manny-rutinel-8th-congressional-district-race/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Denver Post|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Dolven24">{{Cite web |last=Dolven|first=Taylor|last2=Paul|first2=Jesse|date=2026-06-04|title=Less than a year ago, Manny Rutinel staked out different positions on healthcare, student debt and fracking|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/06/04/manny-rutinel-changed-positions-healthcare-student-debt-fracking/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref> Rutinel supports ending the war in Iran through a war powers resolution.<ref name="Paul26" /><ref name="Website-16" />

=== Congressional limitations ===
Rutinel supports term limits for all public offices.<ref name="Paul27">{{Cite web |last=Paul|first=Jesse|last2=Eason|first2=Brian|date=2026-10-21|title=Where Gabe Evans, Manny Rutinel stand on the key issues in the 8th Congressional District|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/21/manny-rutinel-gabe-evans-voter-guide-colorado-district-8/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref> Rutinel also supports a ban on stock trading by members of Congress.<ref name="Kim15">{{Cite web |last=Kim|first=Caitlyn|date=2026-09-25|title=8th Congressional District: Democrat Manny Rutinel|url=https://www.cpr.org/2026/09/25/vg-2026-manny-rutinel-voter-guide/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=Colorado Public Radio|language=en}}</ref><ref name="Website-17">{{Cite web |date=2026-10-22|title=Manny Rutinel leans hard into anti-Trumpism in 8th District race — while pivoting away from his activist past|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2026/10/22/manny-rutinel-8th-congressional-district-race/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Denver Post|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Dolven16">{{Cite web |last=Dolven|first=Taylor|date=2026-05-28|title=Where Shannon Bird and Manny Rutinel stand on the issues in Colorado’s 8th Congressional District primary|url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/05/28/manny-rutinel-shannon-bird-colorado-primary-issue-guide/|access-date=2026-10-23|website=The Colorado Sun|language=en-US}}</ref> Rutinel supports a ban on former members of Congress working as lobbyists.<ref name="Dolven16" />
